slides.texte_overlay:
Underrated skills that will make
you unforgettable in any room
Learn to enter a room calmly. Pause at the door, look around, smile at whoever you know. Don't rush to the corner or grab your phone. The guy who arrives relaxed is the one everyone looks at.
Learn to compliment the host out loud. "This place looks amazing, you did all this?" Hosts are nervous at their own parties. The guest who makes them feel good is the one invited back.
Learn to tell one short, good story. Under a minute, a strange start, a funny end. Practice it once. When the room goes quiet, you'll be the one who gets everyone laughing again.
Learn to notice who's alone. The friend of a friend standing by the snacks. Walk over. "Hey, I'm Sam, how do you know everyone?" One kind move like that and you're the guy they talk about later.
Learn to leave a conversation smoothly. "I'm going to say hi to the host, great talking to you." Leaving well is a skill. Hanging around too long is how good conversations go stale.
Learn to remember one name from every group. Then use it later. "Lucas, did you end up booking that trip?" People feel seen, and they remember the guy who remembered them.
Bring something to talk about. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and you can join any conversation in the room. Range is what makes people remember you.
